messages:
maya: quick sanity check — gpt3.5-lite bring-up results look inconsistent across regions. us-east H100 (flashv3 q8) p99 ~18ms, eu-west H100 (flashv3 q8) p99 ~32ms. same model/quant. anyone seen region-specific kernel slowdowns?

diego: are these from the same kernel build + docker image? and sequence length/distribution the same?

maya: same image tag, same quant artifact. seq distribution: most requests ~256 tokens, micro-bench used seq=256/1024. uploaded a quick spreadsheet: https://our-perf/redwood/gpt3.5-lite/kernels-1965 (view-only)

bench-bot: automated summary: us-east H100 flashv3 q8 B=8 seq=256 throughput=850 tok/s p99=18ms; eu-west H100 flashv3 q8 B=8 seq=256 throughput=420 tok/s p99=32ms. env diff: kernel=flashv3-2026-03-10, triton=2.20.0, cuda=12.1

lucas: two quick hypotheses: (1) vendor kernel fallback in eu-west for certain shapes (check triton logs), (2) noisy neighbor or PCIe topology differences + NVLink configuration across chassis. did you see any "vendor_fallback" messages in the runtime logs?

maya: yes saw intermittent snippet in eu-west logs: "KernelSelector: vendor_fallback=true for layer 7-12". Not consistent every run.

anya: if vendor fallback is the issue, we should try: (a) run with explicit kernel override to force flashv3 for a run, (b) try flashv2 for comparison, (c) sweep batch size. Also consider routing policy: small sequences -> flashv3, long sequences -> vendor/kernel-fallback safe path. Example routing snippet: `route: if seq<=512 -> kernel=flashv3 else -> kernel=vendor`

diego: can you paste the bench command you used? I'll run a microbench in eu-west with `--trace-kernel-selection`.

maya: command I used: ```bash
python infra/bench.py --model gpt3.5-lite --kernel flashv3 --quant q8 --batch 8 --seq 256 --runs 200 --image-tag prod-20260311
```

infra-bot: note — eu-west pool has mixed generations (some H100s in chassis with older firmware). network egress latency difference ~0.9ms median vs us-east on those AZs.

diego: I'm launching microbench with two variants now: (A) force flashv3, (B) force vendor-triton. adding `--trace-kernel-selection` & `--no-prefetch` to be safe. will share results in ~15m.

bench-bot: (after run) eu-west results: forced-flashv3 B=8 seq=256 throughput=810 tok/s p99=26ms; forced-vendor B=8 seq=256 throughput=430 tok/s p99=31ms. trace shows kernel switch spikes on kv-cache refill layers.

lucas: that suggests flashv3 still better than vendor but worse than us-east baseline. compare low-level kernel times for the attention op — looks like one kernel launch is being serialized on some H100s in eu-west. check `nvidia-smi topo -m` and driver messages.

maya: ran `nvidia-smi topo -m` on a sample host in eu-west — shows mixed NVLink connectivity for one socket. I'll open infra ticket to flag those nodes for deeper hardware check.

anya: operationally, for rollout plan we should: 1) add kernel-selection hysteresis (avoid oscillation), 2) fallback policy that prefers flashv2 for seq>1024, 3) regional routing: if p99 on a lane exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive checks, route new requests to alternative region until remediation.

diego: agreed. small experimental change first: add a kernel-override flag in the model config so we can force flashv3 on a subset of traffic and compare real traffic impact.

maya: i'll implement override flag + add an eval suite to compare quality and perf side-by-side. action items: [infra: isolate eu-west bad hosts], [eng-ml: add kernel-override rollout], [ops: add regional hysteresis rule].

bench-bot: created perf run dashboard: https://dash.redwood/perf/1965123456 and infra ticket INF-8292 created for node health.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short post in #eng-ml with the plan and a canary window. :thumbsup:
